lessons.title: Draw Your First Square
lessons.goal: Use a Python loop to draw a four-sided square.

avatar.text: Today Python will become our digital pencil. We will tell a turtle how to move and turn.

flow.title: How a square works
flow.body:
A square has **4 equal sides** and **4 right-angle turns**.

Our turtle will repeat two commands:

1. Move forward
2. Turn left 90 degrees

avatar.text: Instead of writing the same commands four times, we can use a loop. The loop repeats one move and one turn for every side.

code_example.code:
import turtle

pen = turtle.Turtle()
pen.color("purple")
pen.pensize(4)
pen.speed(0)

for side in range(4):
    pen.forward(120)
    pen.left(90)

print("Square complete!")
code_example.description: Watch me import Turtle, create a purple pen, and repeat the square instructions four times.
code_example.explanation: range(4) makes the loop run four times. Each time, the turtle moves 120 steps and turns left 90 degrees.
code_example.starterCode:

avatar.text: Look at the Turtle canvas. Four equal moves and four 90-degree turns made a complete square.

question.question: Complete and run the Python Turtle program so it draws a square using a loop that repeats four times.
question.explanation: A square needs four repetitions, with a 90-degree turn after every side.

code_example.code:
import turtle

pen = turtle.Turtle()
pen.speed(0)

# This example draws a triangle
for side in range(3):
    pen.forward(100)
    pen.left(120)
code_example.description: First, see how a loop can draw a triangle by repeating three times.
code_example.explanation: The same pattern works for a square, but a square needs four repeats and 90-degree turns.
